Says “warsh”\.

Says the names “Don” and “Dawn” the same\.

Says “y’all”\.

Says the words “pen” and “pin” differently\.

Says “caramel” with two syllables \(like “car\-mul”\)\.

# Review from Week 1



* LIN 211 = basic introduction to linguistics designed for non\-majors
* Textbook =  _Linguistics: Why it matters _ by Geoffrey Pullum
* We will use Canvas extensively
* Echo 360 = where you can find lecture slides\, keep notes\, ask questions\, mark slides as confusing\, and participate in lecture
  * So\, you must bring your device to class\!
  * Make sure it is charged\, you know how to use it\, and you don’t use it for non\-class stuff\!
* Review the syllabus and detailed schedule on Canvas for more info on expectations and requirements in the class

---




* Linguistics is the study of language
  * ≠ learning many languages
  * ≠ studying a language with the goal of learning to communicate in it
  * ≠ being the grammar police
* Scientific\, systematic exploration of how language works
  * Includes the study of the  _structure_  of language \(how do we make a sentence?\) and the  _use_  of language \(how do we speak with one another?\)
  * Linguists are interested in  __descriptive grammar__ \, not focused on  __prescriptive grammar__
::: {.notes}

Can refer back to the group activity, if relevant
Prescriptive rules are often trivial, historical, and absurdly motivated
Often can connect to social attitudes against groups


:::
